CONCLUSIONS: There is no obvious regulation of the number of glucocorticoid_receptor by plasma_cortisol_concentration cortisol in vivo. Infection and replication of Tat-_human_immunodeficiency_virus : genetic analyses of LTR and tat_mutation in . Reduced mitogenic_stimulation of peripheral_blood_mononuclear_cell as a prognostic parameter for the course of breast_cancer : a prospective_longitudinal_study. PHA-induced_proliferation PHA of PBMC dropped significantly in patient who received adjuvant chemotherapy consisting of cyclophosphamide, methotrexate and fluorouracil (CMF) after an observation_period of 6 months (P < 0.01), but not in patient under adjuvant treatment with tamoxifen only. After an additional 6 months (i.e. 12 months after surgery), PHA-induced_proliferation PHA of PBMC was similar in patient after adjuvant_chemotherapy with CMF and in those receiving continued adjuvant_tamoxifen_treatment tamoxifen (P > 0.1), but in all patient still significantly decreased as compared with healthy controls (P < 0.001). When data obtained preoperatively and after 12 months were compared, it was found that out of 23 patient whose PBMC had experienced a drop in their PHA-induced_proliferation PHA, 14 (61%) had developed metastatic_disease within the subsequent 24 months (i.e. 36 months after surgery). Distinct roles of the molecular chaperone_hsp90 in modulating dioxin receptor function via the basic helix-loop-helix and PAS_domain. Constitutive NF-kappa_B was not maintained by autocrine action of cytokine TNF, interleukin_6, interleukin 10, granulocyte-macrophage_colony-stimulating_factor or macrophage_colony-stimulating_factor, since neutralizing antibodies did not reduce constitutive DNA-binding_activity. CAG_repeat_length_variation in sperm from a patient with Kennedy's_disease. Increasing RA concentrations reduced the D3_concentration D3 required for monocyte_differentiation. Cells treated with 5 nM D3 showed little response, but differentiated maximally with 5 nM D3 and 10 nM RA. The D3 analogs MC903, EB1089 and KH1060 were more potent inducers of monocyte_differentiation. The extent to which analog_activity was increased after cotreatment with RA was inversely related to potency. Twenty-four hour treatment with 10 nM RA_primed_cell RA for response to 5 nM D3 ; the reverse sequence being ineffective. Priming with 10 nM RA, or subsequent treatment with D3 (5 nM), did not alter expression of mRNA encoding receptor for D3 (VDR), RA (RAR_alpha) or 9-CIS_RA RA (). BCL-6 and the molecular_pathogenesis of B-cell_lymphoma. The results presented identify the first genetic_lesion associated with DLCL, the most clinically relevant form of NHL. Although no proof yet exists of a role for these lesions in DLCL_pathogenesis DLCL, the feature of the BCL-6_gene_product BCL-6, its specific pattern of expression in B_cell, and the clustering of lesions disrupting its regulatory domain strongly suggest that deregulation of BCL-6_expression BCL-6 may contribute to DLCL development. A more precise definition of the role of BCL-6 in normal and neoplastic_B-cell_development is the goal of ongoing study of transgenic_mouse engineered either to express BCL-6 under heterologous_promoter or lacking BCL-6_function BCL-6 due to targeted deletions. In addition to contributing to the understanding of DLCL_pathogenesis DLCL, the identification of BCL-6_lesion BCL-6 may have relevant clinical implications. DLCL represent a heterogeneous group of neoplasm which are treated homogeneously despite the fact that only 50% of patient experience long-term_disease-free_survival (Schneider et al. 1990). The fact that BCL-6_rearrangement BCL-6 identify biologically and clinically distinct subsets of DLCL suggests that these lesions may be useful as markers in selection of differential therapeutic strategies based on different risk groups. Furthermore, the BCL-6_rearrangement BCL-6 can be used to identify and monitor the malignant_clone with sensitive PCR-based_technique. Since clinical remission has been observed in a significant fraction of DLCL cases, these markers may serve as critical tools for sensitive monitoring of minimal residual_disease and early diagnosis of relapse (Gribben et al. 1993).

Pancreatic development and maturation of the islet_B_cell. Studies of pluripotent_islet_culture. pancreas_organogenesis pancreas is a highly regulated process, in which two anlage evaginate from the primitive_gut. They later fuse, and, under the influence of the surrounding mesenchyme, the mature_organ develops, being mainly composed of . Early buds are characterized by a branching morphogenesis of the ductal_epithelium from which bud to eventually form the two other compartments. The three compartments are thought to be of common endodermal_origin ; in contrast to earlier hypotheses, which suggested that the endocrine compartment was of neuroectodermal_origin. It is thus generally believed that the pancreatic_endocrine-lineage possesses the ability to mature along a differentiation_pathway that shares many characteristics with those of neuronal_differentiation. During recent years, studies of insulin-gene_regulation insulin-gene and, in particular, the tissue-specific_transcriptional_control of insulin-gene_activity insulin-gene have provided information on pancreas_development pancreas in general. The present review summarizes these findings, with a special focus on our own studies on pluripotent_endocrine_culture of rat_pancreas.

Generation of CD1+RelB+_dendritic_cell and tartrate-resistant_acid_phosphatase-positive_osteoclast-like_multinucleated_giant_cell from human_monocyte. However, the monocyte-derived_DC DC were not terminally_differentiated_cell ; they could still convert to macrophage in response to M-CSF. tumor_necrosis_factor-alpha (TNF-alpha) stimulated the terminal_differentiation of the DC by downregulating the expression of the M-CSF_receptor M-CSF, cfms_mRNA, and aborting the potential to convert to macrophage. Taken together, these results provide a new aspect to our knowledge of monocyte differentiation and provide evidence that human_monocyte monocyte are flexible in their differentiation_potential and are precursors not only of macrophage but also of CD1+relB+DC and TRAP-positive_MGC. T-cell-directed_TAL-1_expression T-cell TAL-1 induces T-cell_malignancy in transgenic_mice. Novel aldosterone_receptor : specificity-conferring mechanism at the level of the cell_membrane. Functional studies in extra-renal,_nonepithelial_cell such as smooth_muscle_cell and more recently circulating human_lymphocyte have provided increasing evidence that aldosterone produces not only classical genomic effects, but also rapid non-genomic effects on transmembrane_electrolyte_movement. These involve activation of the sodium/proton-exchanger of the cell_membrane at very low, physiological concentrations of aldosterone with an acute onset within 1-2 minutes. A second_messenger_cascade involved is the inositol-1,4,5-trisphosphate/calcium_pathway inositol-1,4,5-trisphosphate calcium which responds over the same rapid time course. Such changes clearly cannot be explained by genomic_mechanism, which are responsible for later effects than the membrane-related_rapid_response. In addition to its rapid time course the unique characteristics of this new pathway for steroid action include a 10000-fold selectivity for aldosterone over cortisol and the ineffectiveness of spironolactone, classical mineralocorticoid_antagonist mineralocorticoid, as antagonists of the response. Subsequently binding sites have been demonstrated in the plasma_membrane of human_lymphocyte which show pharmacological(aldosterone specificity) and kinetic (high turnover) properties identical with those of the rapid aldosterone effects in the same cells. SDS-PAGE_analysis of the receptor_protein has shown a molecular_weight of approximately 50_kD. The present paper reviews the data supporting a new, two-step model for non-genomic and genomic aldosterone effects. It also suggests a novel specificity-conferring_mechanism for mineralocorticoid_action at the membrane_level.

Cloning and characterization of NF-ATc and NF-ATp : the cytoplasmic component of NF-AT. Present evidence indicates a pathway of signal_transmission in T_cell that is outlined in figure 1. This in turn leads to the nuclear association of the cytosolic_component of NF-ATc. The activation of calcineurin and the nuclear_import of NF-ATc can both be blocked by cyclosporin_A or FK506 in complex with their respective immunophilin. Although NF-ATp copurifies with NF-ATc, there is as yet no understanding of how NF-ATp is functioning in vivo. [Molecular mechanisms of age-related_lymphocyte_dysfunction ] Aging is classically accompanied by a dysregulation of the immunologic_machinery. As a consequence, the immune_response developed in senescent_organism is usually inappropriate, often inefficient, sometimes aberrant, and potentially detrimental. The age-associated_immune_dysfunction may be implicated to some degree in the extreme susceptibility of the elderly to infection and neoplasia and may even participate in various aspects of senescence. The current understanding of the molecular_mechanism underlying immunosenescence is still fragmentary. The most extensively studied phenomenon is the progressive decline in the proliferative_capacity of T_lymphocyte with aging. The loss of proliferative potential in response to antigenic challenge is a characteristic feature of immune senescence. It is directly implicated in the emergence of the age-related_immune_deficiency. The purpose of this review is to show how the accumulation of various biochemical_lesion with advancing age leads to the failure of a critical cell function, namely the activation-induced_lymphocyte_proliferation. The biochemical_modification responsible for the defect in transduction and execution of the proliferative signal are analyzed as a function of age. The multiple alterations observed on the various biochemical_pathway may appear as a consequence of a unique deleterious mechanism more fundamentally related to the process of senescence such as the inability to cope with oxidative_stress.

Analysis of the ligand-binding_domain of human_retinoic_acid_receptor_alpha by site-directed_mutagenesis. All conserved cysteine and arginine_residue in this domain were mutated_by_site-directed_mutagenesis, and the mutant_protein were characterized by blocking_reaction, ligand-binding_experiment, transactivation_assay, and protease_mapping protease. Interestingly, residue_C-235 C-235 is specifically important in antagonist binding. With respect to arginine_residue, only the two single_mutation of R-276 and R-394 to alanine showed a dramatic decrease of agonist and antagonist binding whereas the R272A_mutation R272A showed only a slight effect. For all other arginine_mutation arginine, no differences in affinity were detectable. The two mutation R217A and R294A caused an increased binding efficiency for antagonists but no change in agonist binding. From these results, we can conclude that electrostatic_interaction of retinoid with the RAR_alpha-LBD RAR_alpha play a significant role in ligand_binding. In addition, antagonists show distinctly different requirements for efficient binding, which may contribute to their interference in the ligand-inducible_transactivation_function of RAR_alpha.

Epstein-Barr_viral_latency is disrupted by the immediate-early_BRLF1_protein through a cell-specific_mechanism. Understanding how viral_latency is disrupted is a central issue in herpesvirus_biology. Epithelial cells are the major site of lytic_EBV_replication EBV within the human_host, and viral reactivation occurs in EBV-associated_nasopharyngeal_carcinoma EBV nasopharyngeal_carcinoma. It is known that expression of a single viral_immediate-early_protein, BZLF1, is sufficient to initiate the switch from latent to lytic_infection in B_cell. cellular_regulation of BZLF1_transcription BZLF1 is therefore thought to play a key role in regulating the stringency of viral_latency. Here we show that, unexpectedly, expression of another viral_immediate-early_protein, BRLF1, can disrupt viral_latency in an epithelial_cell-specific_fashion. Therefore, the mechanisms leading to disruption of EBV latency appear to be cell-type specific.

CTL_recognition of an altered_peptide associated with asparagine_bond_rearrangement asparagine. Implications for immunity and vaccine_design. The CTL specifically recognized the succinimide-containing_peptide showing only weak cross-reactivity at high concentrations of the parent_peptide containing unmodified_asparagine. Similarly, CTL raised against the parent_peptide did not recognize the succinimide_derivative of this peptide. Naturally processed forms of these structures are likely to occur given the importance and frequency of deamidation both in vitro and in vivo. Moreover, since succinimide_intermediate of deamidated_peptide peptide can occasionally be very stable, these peptide have the potential to act as altered_self-Ags with significant implications for autoimmunity. In addition, unwanted and potentially hazardous specificities may be elicited when using synthetic_peptide in subunit vaccines in which succinimide_residue may form spontaneously during storage or chemical_synthesis.

Monoallelic expression of Pax5 : a paradigm for the haploinsufficiency of mammalian_Pax_gene ? It is generally assumed that most mammalian_gene are transcribed from both allele. Indeed, the vast majority of human_disease_syndrome and engineered mutations in the mouse_genome are recessive, indicating that recessiveness is the 'default' state. However, a minority of genes are semi-dominant, as heterozygous loss-of-function_mutation in these genes leads to phenotypic_abnormality. This condition, known as haploinsufficiency, has been described for five of the nine mammalian_Pax_gene, which are associated with mouse_developmental_mutant and human_disease_syndrome. Pax5 is predominantly transcribed from only one of its two allele in early_B-lymphoid_progenitor and mature_B_cell, while it transiently switches to a biallelic mode of transcription in . As a consequence, B-lymphoid_tissue are mosaic with regard to the transcribed allele, and heterozygous_mutation of Pax5 therefore results in deletion of B_lymphocyte expressing only the mutant_allele allele. In this review, we discuss different models accounting for the haploinsufficiency of mammalian_Pax_gene Pax_gene, provide further evidence in support of the allele-specific_regulation allele of Pax5 and discuss the implication of these findings in the context of the recent literature describing the stochastic_activation and monoallelic_activation of other hematopoietic_gene.

transcriptional_inhibition by interleukin-6 of the class_A_macrophage_scavenger_receptor in macrophage derived from human_peripheral_monocyte and the THP-1_monocytic_cell_line THP-1. cell_activation and apoptosis by bacterial_lipoprotein through toll-like_receptor-2. apoptosis is implicated in the generation and resolution of inflammation in response to bacterial_pathogen. Possible differences in the mechanism(s) of action of different glucocorticoid_hormone_compound. Distinctive expression pattern of the BCL-6_protein BCL-6 in nodular_lymphocyte_predominance_Hodgkin's_disease. The involvement of p23, hsp90, and immunophilin in the assembly of progesterone_receptor_complex. Block of granulocytic_differentiation of 32Dcl3_cell by AML1/ETO(MTG8) but not by highly expressed Bcl-2. Host defense mechanisms triggered by microbial_lipoprotein through toll-like_receptor. Novel therapies for inflammatory_bowel_disease. Looking back at successes and failures in newer approaches to treating IBD, it is tempting--although still difficult--to draw conclusions about pathogenesis. When a therapy proves effective, do clinicians truly know how it works? Even with a therapy as specific as anti-TNF_antibody, it is not clear if the benefit is attributable to simple binding and clearance of TNF-alpha or to binding on the cell_surface and subsequent deletion of the activated_macrophage. When a drug appears to be less effective than preclinical_model suggest, can failures in effectiveness from delivery or dosing be differentiated? The disappointing results of clinical trials with IL-10 --so at odds with the prediction of benefit from animal_model --bring into question the validity of those models as well as the soundness of design of the clinical_trial on which efficacy of IL-10 is judged. The variability of response even to the most narrowly targeted agents suggests that these diseases are far more heterogeneous in human than in their murine_counterpart. Clinicians are only just beginning to recognize subclinical_marker of response, and it may soon be possible to predict response on the basis of genetic_composition. For the moment, however, the field of pharmacogenetic is embryonic. Challenges in developing new therapeutic_strategy include not only identifying novel agents, but also improving the definitions of clinical endpoints and defining efficacy at the biologic level. Only through considered evaluation of clinical evidence may clinician determine which therapies should remain novelties and which should become an accepted part of the armamentarium.

The functional synergy between IL-12 and IL-2 involves p38_mitogen-activated_protein_kinase and is associated with the augmentation of STAT_serine_phosphorylation serine. estrone potentiates myeloid_cell_differentiation : a role for 17_beta-hydroxysteroid_dehydrogenase in modulating hemopoiesis. Modulation of the immune_response and tumor_growth by activated Ras. As a result of its transforming_ability, activated_Ras is expressed in a great number of cancer. The presence of ras mutations has been correlated with a poor prognosis and negative clinical outcome. Several new functions of Ras, such as downregulation of major_histocompatibility_complex_molecule, upregulation of certain cytokine, growth_factor and degradative_enzyme have been uncovered in the last decade. Additionally, mutated_Ras can also serve as a primary target for the development of immunotherapy or drug_therapy. This review will discuss the mechanisms by which Ras expressing tumor are able to evade destruction by the immune_system and enhance their growth and metastatic_potential. It will further elaborate on the attempts to develop successful immunotherapy and drug_therapy targeting Ras expressing tumor.

glucocorticoid_receptor, fibromyalgia and low_back_pain. Recently, fibromyalgia (FMS) was shown to be a disorder associated with an altered functioning of the stress_response_system. We suggested that negative feedback of cortisol could be deranged. Therefore we investigated the properties and function of the glucocorticoid_receptor (GR) in FMS patient and compared the results with those of healthy_persons and patient with chronic low_back_pain (LBP a localized pain condition). Forty primary FMS patient (F:M = 36:4), 28 LBP patient (25:3) and 14 (12:2) healthy, sedentary control persons were recruited for the study. urinary_free_cortisol_excretion in FMS and LBP patient was lower compared to controls. Only FMS patient displayed lower CBG and basal_serum_cortisol_concentration cortisol when compared to controls. However, plasma_free_cortisol_concentration cortisol were similar in the three groups. There was no difference in the number of GR per cell among the three groups(FMS : 6498 +/- 252, LBP : 6625 +/- 284, control : 6576 +/- 304), but the dissociation constant (Kd) of the FMS (14.5 +/- 0.9 nmol/l) and LBP (14.7 +/- 1.3 nmol/l) subjects was significantly higher than that of the control (10.9 +/- 0.8 nmol/l) (p <.05). The maximal stimulation of the lymphocyte, as measured by the maximal_thymidine_incorporation thymidine (in the absence of cortisol) in the FMS group was approximately 1.5 times higher (p <.05) than in the control or LBP_group. The ED50 (the cortisol concentration giving 50% inhibition of the thymidine_incorporation thymidine), however, was identical in all three groups. We conclude that FMS patient have a mild hypocortisolemia, increased cortisol feedback resistance in combination probably with a reduced CRH_synthesis CRH or release in the hypothalamus. The role of the GR and mineralocorticoid_receptor (MR) in the CRH regulation in the FMS patient remains to be solved.

HLA_binding_characteristic and generation of cytotoxic_lymphocyte against peptide derived from oncogenic_protein. AIMS AND BACKGROUND: Structurally altered proteins (derived from chromosomal_translocation or gene_mutation) can be considered tumor specific antigens and represent an attractive target for a T-cell_mediated_response. T lymphocytes recognize antigens in the form of peptide bound to HLA-molecule. MATERIALS AND METHODS: peptide derived from oncogenic_protein were screened for the presence of HLA_binding_motif ; actual binding were evaluated by HLA_stabilization_experiment using transfectants and specific anti-HLA_antibody. Specific lymphocyte were induced by in_vitro_peptide_sensitization and screened by thymidine_uptake thymidine or cellular_cytotoxic_assay. RESULTS: We identified peptide derived from EWS/FLI-1_fusion_protein and from mutated_K-RAS_protein (encompassing respectively the fusion_point and the mutation at position_12) that showed binding_motif for HLA-Cw*0702 and HLA-A3 respectively. The actual binding of these peptide was analysed in a stabilization_assay. We detected binding for the EWS/FLI-1_peptide and for 5_RAS_peptide peptide (1 wild type and 4 mutated). The effect of temperature, beta_2-microglobulin (beta_2-m) and fetal_calf_serum (FCS) on the binding and the stability of the HLA/peptide_complex was studied. A low temperature (26 degrees C) increased the binding both in HLA-A3 and HLA-Cw*0702, while FCS reduced it. beta_2-m increased the binding to the HLA-A3_molecule HLA-A3 but did not influence the binding to the HLA-Cw*0702. The stability of already formed complexed was somewhat different in the HLA-A3 and HLA-Cw*0702_system HLA-Cw*0702 : both were more stable at 26 degrees C than at 37 degrees C but while the beta_2-m and FCS did not influence the stability of the HLA-A3/peptide_complex HLA-A3, they seemed to cause opposite effects in the HLA-Cw*0702_system HLA-Cw*0702 (beta_2-m stabilized and FCS destabilized the complex). Finally, we were able to generate a specific CD8+_CTL_line against a K-RAS_mutated_peptide. CONCLUSIONS: Although binding_motif and actual HLA binding can be detected in several cases, the generation of a cellular response is infrequent, confirming that HLA binding is necessary but not sufficient to obtain an in_vitro_response. Further optimization of culture conditions, type of Antigen_Presenting_Cell (APC), peptide, use of stabilizers like beta_2-m are still needed.

OCA-B is a functional analog of VP16 but targets a separate surface of the Oct-1_POU_domain [published erratum appears in Mol Cell Biol 1998 Apr;18(4):2430] OCA-B is a B-cell-specific_coregulator of the broadly expressed POU_domain_transcription_factor Oct-1. late_gene_expression from the Epstein-Barr_virus does not require DNA_replication in cis. Late gene expression follows and is dependent upon lytic_replication of the viral_genome. In addition, these promoters respond only indirectly to the viral_immediate-early_transactivator, ZEBRA. The A-myb_transcription_factor A-myb in . The myb_family of transcription_factor has been strongly implicated in the regulation of cell growth and differentiation in the haematopoietic_system. The v-myb_oncogene, carried by avian_defective_retrovirus, causes leukaemia in the chicken and transforms haematopoietic_cell in vitro. Its normal cellular equivalent c-myb, has been shown to promote the proliferation and block the differentiation of haematopoietic_cell in several experimental models and is required for fetal_haematopoiesis. Two other members of the family have been cloned more recently, A-myb and B-myb, which show sequence homology with c-myb in several domains, of which the DNA_binding_domain as well as other regulatory_domain. Both have been shown to be transcription_factor. B-myb is also involved in the control of proliferation and differentiation, but, unlike c-myb, it is expressed in many cell types. The third member of the family, A-myb, shows the most restricted pattern of expression, suggesting a very specific role for this transcription_factor. A-myb is expressed in a subpopulation of normal_B_lymphocyte activated in vivo and localised in the germinal center of peripheral_lymphoid_organ and is not detected at significant levels in all other mature or immature_haematopoietic_population studied, including bone_marrow_cell, T_lymphocyte, granulocyte, monocyte, either at rest or after in_vitro_activation. These studies indicate that A-myb plays a role during a narrow window of normal_B_cell_differentiation normal_B_cell. A-myb_expression A-myb has also been studied in a wide range of neoplastic_B_cell, representing the whole spectrum of B_cell_differentiation. A-myb is strongly expressed in Burkitt's_lymphoma (BL) and slg+_B-acute_lymphoblastic_leukaemia leukaemia (B-ALL) and not in all other leukaemia/lymphoma leukaemia tested, with the exception of a subset of CLL (about 25% of cases). It is intriguing that the A-myb_genome A-myb has been localised relatively close to the c-myc_gene on chromosome_8, suggesting that the c-myc translocation in BL and B-ALL may affect A-myb_transcription A-myb. Studies are in progress to investigate the functional relationship between A-myb and c-myc, particularly in the context of BL_cell BL and to determine whether A-myb is deregulated in these cells.

Construction and biological characterization of an interleukin-12_fusion_protein (Flexi-12): delivery to acute_myeloid_leukemic_blast using adeno-associated_virus. Interleukin-12 (IL-12) is a cytokine that exhibits pleiotropic_effect on lymphocyte and natural_killer_cell and has been shown to have promise for the immunotherapy of cancer. The combination of the immune_costimulatory_molecule B7.1 and IL-12 has been shown to be synergistic for T_cell_activation. By transfecting tumor cells with both , it may be possible to use these modified targets as vaccine. A major obstacle in designing a vector to deliver these genes results from the structure of IL-12. This presents several problems in vectors, particularly those in which additional genes, either a co-stimulatory_gene or a selectable marker, are inserted. reactive_oxygen_specie and antioxidant in inflammatory_disease. Mutations in the TSC2_gene : analysis of the complete coding sequence using the protein_truncation_test (PTT). Mutations in the TSC2_gene on chromosome_16p13.3 are responsible for approximately 50% of familial_tuberous_sclerosis (TSC). The gene has 41_small_exon spanning 45_kb of genomic_DNA and encoding a 5.5_kb_mRNA. Three overlapping PCR_product, covering the complete coding sequence of mRNA, were generated from lymphoblastoid_cell_line, translated into 35S-methionine_labelled_protein, and analysed by SDS-PAGE. PCR_product showing PTT shifts were directly sequenced, and mutations confirmed by restriction_enzyme_digestion where possible. Six PTT_shift PTT were identified. Five of these were caused by mutations predicted to produce a truncated_protein : (i) a sporadic case showed a 32_bp_deletion in exon_11, and a mutant_mRNA without exon_11 was produced; the normal exon 10 was also spliced out; (ii) a sporadic case had a 1_bp_deletion in exon_12 (1634delT); (iii) a TSC2-linked_mother_and_daughter_pair TSC2 had a G-->T transversion in exon_23 (G2715T) introducing a cryptic splice site causing a 29 bp truncation of mRNA from exon_23 ; (iv) a sporadic case showed a 2_bp_deletion in exon_36 ; (v) a sporadic case showed a 1_bp_insertion disrupting the donor splice site of exon_37 (5007+2insA), resulting in the use of an upstream_exonic_cryptic_splice_site to cause a 29_bp_truncation of mRNA from exon_37. In one case, the PTT shift was explained by in-frame splicing out of exon_10, in the presence of a normal_exon_10_genomic_sequence. Alternative splicing of exon_10 of the TSC2_gene may be a normal variant. Three 3rd_base_substitution_polymorphism were also detected during direct sequencing of PCR_product. Confirmed mutations were identified in 28% of the families studied and on the assumption that half of the sporadic cases should have TSC2_mutation, a crude estimate of the detection rate would be 60%. This compares favourably with other screening methods used for TSC2, notably SSCP, and since PTT involves much less work it may be the method of choice.

The role of nuclear_factor-kappa_B in cytokine_gene_regulation cytokine_gene. transcription_factor are DNA-binding_protein that regulate gene_expression. nuclear_factor-kappa_B (NF-kappa_B) is a critical transcription_factor for maximal expression of many cytokine that are involved in the pathogenesis of inflammatory_disease, such as adult_respiratory_distress_syndrome (ARDS) and sepsis_syndrome. Activation and regulation of NF-kappa_B are tightly controlled by a group of inhibitory_protein (I_kappa_B) that sequester NF-kappa_B in the cytoplasm of immune/inflammatory_effector_cell. Liberated NF-kappa_B migrates to the nucleus, where it binds to specific_promoter_site and activates gene_transcription. The activation of NF-kappa_B initiates both extracellular and intracellular regulatory_event that result in autoregulation of the inflammatory_cascade through modulation of NF-kappa_B_activation NF-kappa_B. Recently, activation of NF-kappa_B has been linked to ARDS and has been shown to be a critical proximal step in the initiation of neutrophilic_inflammation in animal_model. Activation of NF-kappa_B can be inhibited in vivo by treatment with antioxidant, corticosteroid, and the induction of endotoxin_tolerance endotoxin. CONCLUSIONS: Our results establish that PI_3-kinase can both positively and negatively regulate T-cell_function, and uncover a previously unrecognized function for PI_3-kinase in T_cell as a selective negative regulator of TCR-signalling_event TCR and therefore as a determinant of T-cell_homeostasis.

Cloning and expression of the glucocorticoid_receptor from the squirrel_monkey (Saimiri_boliviensis_boliviensis), a glucocorticoid-resistant primate. The control of lytic_replication of Epstein-Barr_virus in B_lymphocyte (Review). Uncontrolled replication of a virus, which is harmful to the host is also disadvantageous to the virus. Most virus cannot compete with the various immune_mechanism and become eliminated in the course of infection. Therefore, only the time between infection and eradication remains for these viruses to proliferate. A few viruses, like the Herpesvirus or the papillomavirus, however, have developed a sophisticated strategy for persisting lifelong, usually asymptomatically in the host, hiding from the immune_system and producing infectious_progeny at the same time. This strategy depends on a separation of latency and the lytic_replication, either by time due to differentiation-dependent_mechanism or by spatial separation as the result of different host cell types. Both are true for the Epstein-Barr_virus (EBV). B_cell and epithelial_cell have a pivotal role in the life cycle of the virus. The former can become latently infected and are thought to be the virus reservoir in vivo, whereas the latter were shown to be permissive for lytic_replication. However, replication of EBV in vivo is controlled primarily by host immune_mechanism selecting for cells that are not permissive for viral replication as the result of a particular set of transcription_factor. These factors control the activity of the regulatory_immediate-early_gene and, in addition, lytic and latent cycle regulatory genes negatively interfere with each other and thus link cellular and viral_gene_regulatory_mechanism viral_gene. Disturbance of both the immune_surveillance as well as viral_gene regulation may result in EBV-associated_disease EBV.

The role of the Ikaros_gene in . The Ikaros_gene, which encodes a family of hemopoietic-specific_zinc_finger_protein, is described as a central regulator of lymphocyte_differentiation. A significant increase in CD4_thymocyte and their immediate precursors is detected, and because these cells lack markers that correlate with positive selection, a deregulation in their maturation process is suggested. Deregulated TCR-mediated_response TCR and the fast kinetics of tumor_development in these mutant_thymocyte implicate Ikaros as a central_tumor_suppressor_gene for the T_cell_lineage. In addition, lack of natural_killer_cell and selective defects in gamma_delta_T_cell and dendritic_antigen-presenting_cell point to Ikaros as an essential factor for the establishment of early branchpoints of the T_cell_pathway. The dominant interference activity of Ikaros_isoform Ikaros unable to bind DNA and their effects in lymphocyte_development suggest that Ikaros works in concert with other factors. The role of Aiolos, a , in lymphoid_differentiation is discussed. A model is proposed that defines Ikaros as the backbone of a complex_regulatory_protein_network that controls cell fate decisions and regulates homeostasis in the hemo-lymphoid_system. Changes in this regulatory network may reflect differentiation and proliferation adjustments made in hemo-lymphoid_progenitors and precursor as they give rise to the cells of our immune_system.

Initiation of proliferation but not of differentiation was followed by a 20- to 25-fold increase in the nuclear level of the DNA_polymerase-associated_processivity_factor_PCNA PCNA and of the proliferation-specific_transcription_factor_E2F1 E2F1. In contrast, induction of differentiation but not of proliferation was followed by a 25- to 30-fold increase in the nuclear level of the tumor_suppressor_protein_p53 (wild type), pRb, and p130/Rb2 and of the p53-dependent_cyclin_kinase_inhibitor p21/Cip1. p53 and p21/Cip1, respectively, inhibit the expression and activation of PCNA, whereas p130 and pRb, respectively, inhibit the expression and activation of E2F1. Inhibition of HIV-1_latency_reactivation HIV-1 by dehydroepiandrosterone (DHEA) and an analog of DHEA. FK506 and ciclosporin : molecular probes for studying intracellular_signal_transduction. As described by Jun Liu, these drugs manifest their effects in an unprecedented fashion. They do not directly intercept intracellular signalling molecules. cell-specific_expression of helix-loop-helix_transcription_factor encoded by the E2A_gene. hypertension in pregnancy. pregnancy-induced_hypertension (PIH) is a frequent cause of maternal and neonatal morbidity and mortality. In the present study we focused on the pathophysiology of PIH, mainly on the role of mineralocorticoid, reversed_blood_pressure_pattern, and the resulting necessity of continuous monitoring of the preeclamptic_mother. Problems of antihypertensive_therapy are discussed and the first results of a pilot study with Urapidil are presented. To examine the role of mineralocorticoid in the pathophysiology of PIH, we studied plasma_aldosterone and 18-hydroxy-corticosterone (18-OH-B) levels in 25 women with PIH and in 25 healthy pregnant women. Furthermore, we evaluated the mineralocorticoid_receptor_(MR)_count mineralocorticoid_receptor MR in mononuclear_leukocyte in the 2 groups. The MR-count was significantly decreased in the PIH -group. The values of plasma_aldosterone and 18-OH-B were also low. These results cannot be explained by receptor down-regulation due to higher level of mineralocorticoid of the zona_glomerulosa. Perhaps deoxycorticosterone or a hitherto unknown mineralocorticoid is responsible for the hypertension and altered MR-status MR. The first results of continuous blood_pressure_measurement with a noninvasive, real-time_blood_pressure_monitor (Finapres) are presented. The comparison of the obtained values with intraarterial_measurement demonstrates a good correlation between the two methods. We also report on the first experiences with Urapidil in the treatment of hypertension in severe_preeclampsia. The data show that hypertension in preeclamptic_women can be treated by Urapidil without side effects or reflex-tachycardia. Further studies will have to prove if Urapidil is suited for prepartal treatment of PIH as well.

Suppression of a cellular_differentiation_program by phorbol_ester coincides with inhibition of binding of a cell-specific_transcription_factor (NF-E2) to an enhancer_element required for expression of an erythroid-specific_gene. TPA induction inhibits the binding of the lineage_limited_transcription_factor NF-E2 to this transcriptional_control_element. Hemin induction appears to nonspecifically increase the expression of transiently transfected genes in K562_cell. Beyond this nonspecific increase in gene expression, hemin_induction hemin acts to increase the activity of the lineage_limited_transcription_factor NF-E2. The divergent effects of hemin and TPA on gene expression in K562_cell are mediated, in part, by their contrasting effects on the transcription_factor NF-E2.

Interleukin-3_expression interleukin-3 by activated_T_cell involves an inducible, T-cell-specific_factor and an octamer_binding_protein. Interleukin-3 (IL-3) is exclusively expressed by activated_T_cell and natural_killer_cell, a function that is tightly controlled both in a lineage-specific and in a stimulation-dependent manner. We have investigated the protein binding characteristics and functional importance of the ACT-1-activating_region of the IL-3 promoter. This region binds an inducible, T-cell-specific_factor over its 5'_end, a site that is necessary for the expression of IL-3 in the absence of other upstream elements. Over its 3'_end, it binds a factor that is ubiquitously and constitutively expressed. This factor is Oct-1 or an immunologically_related_octamer-binding_protein, and it plays a role in coordinating the activity of several regulatory_element. These characteristics make the ACT-1_site analogous to the activating ARRE-1_site in the IL-2_promoter. Furthermore, and despite a lack of sequence homology, the promoters of IL-3 and IL-2 share an organizational pattern of regulatory elements that is likely to be important for the T-cell-specific_expression of these genes.

aldosterone-specific_membrane_receptor and rapid non-genomic actions of mineralocorticoid. Functional studies in extrarenal,_non-epithelial_cell such as smooth_muscle_cell and more recently circulating_human_lymphocyte human_lymphocyte have provided increasing evidence that aldosterone produces not only classical genomic effects, but also rapid, non-genomic effects on transmembrane_electrolyte_movement electrolyte. A second messenger cascade involved is the inositol_1,4,5-trisphosphate/calcium_pathway inositol_1,4,5-trisphosphate calcium which responds over the same rapid time course. Such changes clearly cannot be explained by genomic_mechanism, which are responsible for later effects than the membrane related rapid responses. The mechanisms underlying these rapid effects of aldosterone on electrolyte have been extensively studied in human_lymphocyte, which thus may represent valuable tools in the delineation of the receptor-effector_mechanism involved. The unique characteristics of this new pathway for steroid_action steroid include its rapid time course, 10,000-fold selectivity for aldosterone over cortisol and the ineffectiveness of spironolactone, classical_mineralocorticoid_antagonist, as antagonists of the response.

SCL and related hemopoietic_helix-loop-helix_transcription_factor helix-loop-helix transcription_factor. Although activated in T_cell_leukemia, expression of SCL and LYL-1 is low or undetectable in normal_T_cell_population. mineralocorticoid_effector_mechanism in preeclampsia. mineralocorticoid_effector_mechanism were evaluated in 29 patient with preeclampsia and in 25 uncomplicated_pregnancy by measurement of plasma_aldosterone, levels of mineralocorticoid_receptor (MR) in mononuclear_leucocyte, and subtraction_potential_difference (SPD ; rectal_minus_oral_values). Mean values for plasma_aldosterone were not different between the two groups, but significant differences were observed for MR (preeclampsia, 81 +/- 44 receptors/cell; controls, 306 +/- 168) and SPD (preeclampsia, 65 +/- 7 mV; controls, 12 +/- 5 mV). leukotriene_B4 transcriptionally activates interleukin-6_expression interleukin-6 involving NK-chi_B and NF-IL6. leukotriene_B4 (LTB4) is a notable participant in inflammation and chemotaxis. cortisol_receptor_resistance : the variability of its clinical presentation and response to treatment. primary_(partial)_cortisol_receptor_resistance cortisol_receptor cortisol was previously reported in a total of 7 patient and 14 asymptomatic_family_member. The development of functionally responsive T_cell. The work reviewed in this article separates T_cell_development into four phases. First is an expansion phase prior to TCR_rearrangement TCR, which appears to be correlated with programming of at least some response genes for inducibility. This phase can occur to some extent outside of the thymus. However, the profound T_cell_deficit of nude_mice indicates that the thymus is by far the most potent site for inducing the expansion per se, even if other sites can induce some response acquisition. Second is a controlled phase of TCR_gene_rearrangement TCR_gene. The details of the regulatory_mechanism that selects particular loci for rearrangement are still not known. It seems that the rearrangement of the TCR_gamma_loci in the gamma_delta_lineage may not always take place at a developmental stage strictly equivalent to the rearrangement of TCR_beta in the alpha_beta_lineage, and it is not clear just how early the two lineages diverge. In the TCR_alpha_beta_lineage alpha_beta_lineage however, the final gene_rearrangement_event rearrangement are accompanied by rapid proliferation and an interruption in cellular_response_gene_inducibility. The loss of conventional_responsivenessp is probably caused by alterations at the level of signaling, and may be a manifestation of the physiological state that is a precondition for selection. Third is the complex process of selection. Whereas peripheral_T_cell T_cell can undergo forms of positive_selection (by antigen-driven clonal expansion) and negative selection (by abortive stimulation leading to anergy or death), neither is exactly the same phenomenon that occurs in the thymic_cortex. negative_selection in the cortex appears to be a suicidal inversion of antigen_responsiveness : instead of turning on IL-2_expression IL-2, the activated_cell destroys its own chromatin. The genes that need to be induced for this response are not yet identified, but it is unquestionably a form of activation. It is interesting that in human and rat, cortical_thymocyte undergoing negative selection can still induce IL-2R_alpha_expression IL-2R_alpha and even be rescued in vitro, if exogenous_IL-2 is provided. Perhaps murine_thymocyte are denied this form of rescue because they shut off IL-2R_beta_chain_expression IL-2R_beta_chain at an earlier stage or because they may be uncommonly Bcl-2_deficient bcl-2 (cf. Sentman et al., 1991; Strasser et al., 1991). Even so, medullary_thymocyte remain at least partially susceptible to negative selection even as they continue to mature.

I_kappa_B/MAD-3 masks the nuclear localization signal of NF-kappa_B_p65 and requires the transactivation_domain to inhibit NF-kappa_B_p65_DNA_binding NF-kappa_B_p65. The active nuclear form of the NF-kappa_B_transcription_factor_complex is composed of two DNA_binding_subunit, NF-kappa_B_p65 and NF-kappa_B_p50, both of which share extensive N-terminal_sequence_homology with the v-rel_oncogene_product. The NF-kappa_B_p65_subunit NF-kappa_B_p65 provides the transactivation_activity in this complex and serves as an intracellular receptor for a cytoplasmic_inhibitor of NF-kappa_B, termed I kappa B. In contrast, NF-kappa_B_p50 alone fails to stimulate kappa_B-directed_transcription, and based on prior in vitro studies, is not directly regulated by I_kappa_B. To investigate the molecular basis for the critical regulatory interaction between NF-kappa_B and I_kappa_B/MAD-3, a series of human_NF-kappa_B_p65_mutant NF-kappa_B_p65 was identified that functionally segregated DNA binding, I_kappa_B-mediated_inhibition I_kappa_B, and I_kappa_B-induced_nuclear_exclusion I_kappa_B of this transcription_factor. Results from in vivo expression studies performed with these NF-kappa_B_p65_mutant revealed the following: 1) I_kappa_B/MAD-3 completely inhibits NF-kappa_B_p65-dependent_transcriptional_activation NF-kappa_B_p65 mediated through the human_immunodeficiency_virus_type_1_kappa_B_enhancer human_immunodeficiency_virus_type_1 in human_T_lymphocyte, 2) the binding of I_kappa_B/MAD-3 to NF-kappa_B_p65 is sufficient to retarget NF-kappa_B_p65 from the nucleus to the cytoplasm, 3) selective deletion of the functional nuclear localization signal present in the Rel_homology_domain of NF-kappa_B_p65 disrupts its ability to engage I_kappa_B/MAD-3, and 4) the unique C-terminus of NF-kappa_B_p65 attenuates its own nuclear localization and contains sequences that are required for I_kappa_B-mediated_inhibition I_kappa_B of NF-kappa_B_p65_DNA_binding_activity NF-kappa_B_p65. Together, these findings suggest that the nuclear localization signal and transactivation_domain of NF-kappa_B_p65 constitute a bipartite system that is critically involved in the inhibitory function of I_kappa_B/MAD-3. Unexpectedly, our in vivo studies also demonstrate that I_kappa_B/MAD-3 binds directly to NF-kappa_B_p50. nuclear_factor of activated_T_cell contains Fos and Jun. The nuclear_factor_NF-AT (ref. 1) is induced in T_cell stimulated through the T-cell_receptor/CD3_complex, and is required for interleukin-2_(IL-2)_gene_induction interleukin-2_(IL-2)_gene interleukin-2 IL-2. On the basis of , we propose that activation of NF-AT occurs in at least two stages: a CsA-sensitive_stage CsA involving modification and/or translocation of the pre-existing NF-AT_complex NF-AT, and a CsA -insensitive stage involving the addition of newly synthesized Fos or Fos/Jun_protein to the pre-existing_complex.

cortisol_resistance in acquired_immunodeficiency_syndrome. [3H]Thymidine incorporation was decreased dose-dependently by dexamethasone in control and patients; the effect was significantly blunted (P less than 0.05) in group 1 patient, which suggests that activation of glucocorticoid_receptor is impaired as a result of the glucocorticoid_receptor_abnormality glucocorticoid_receptor. In conclusion, AIDS_patient with hypercortisolism and clinical features of peripheral resistance to glucocorticoid are characterized by abnormal_glucocorticoid_receptor on lymphocyte. Resistance to glucocorticoid implies a complex change in immune-endocrine_function, which may be important in the course of immunodeficiency_syndrome.

A novel primer_extension_method to detect the number of CAG_repeat in the androgen_receptor_gene in families with X-linked_spinal_atrophy and bulbar_muscular_atrophy. X-linked spinal and bulbar muscular atrophy (SBMA), an adult-onset form of motor neuron disease, was recently reported to be caused by amplification of the CAG repeats in the androgen_receptor_gene. We report here a simple and rapid strategy to detect the precise number of the CAG. After the DNA_fragment containing the CAG_repeat is amplified by the polymerase_chain_reaction, a primer_extension is carried out; the extension of the end-labelled_reverse_primer adjacent to 3'_end of CAG_repeats stops at the first T after CAG_repeat with the incorporation of dideoxy_ATP in the reaction mixture. resulting in tissue_factor_expression tissue_factor and relevance to septic_shock. Cells of monocyte lineage serve as effector_cell in the cellular_immune_response. phorbol_ester reduces constitutive_nuclear_NF_kappa_B NF_kappa_B and inhibits HIV-1_production HIV-1 in mature_human_monocytic_cell monocytic_cell. NF_kappa_B is a potent mediator of specific gene expression in human monocytes and has been shown to play a role in transcription of the HIV-1 genome in promonocytic leukemias. Finally, TPA addition to monocyte infected with HIV-1 inhibited HIV-1_replication HIV-1, as determined by reverse_transcriptase_assay reverse_transcriptase, in a concentration-dependent manner. These results are in striking contrast to the increase in nuclear NF_kappa_B and HIV-1 replication induced by phorbol_ester in promonocytic_leukemia_cells_U937 and HL-60, and emphasize the importance of studying cytokine_regulation cytokine of HIV-1 in normal_monocyte.

A mechanism for the antiinflammatory_effect of corticosteroid : the glucocorticoid_receptor regulates leukocyte_adhesion to endothelial_cell and expression of endothelial-leukocyte_adhesion_molecule_1 and intercellular_adhesion_molecule_1. corticosteroid are the preeminent_antiinflammatory_agent although the molecular_mechanism that impart their efficacy have not been defined. The endothelium plays a critical role in inflammation by directing circulating_leukocyte into extravascular_tissue by expressing adhesive_molecule for leukocyte [e.g., endothelial-leukocyte_adhesion_molecule_1 (ELAM-1) and intercellular_adhesion_molecule_1 (ICAM-1)]. We therefore determined whether corticosteroid suppress inflammation by inhibiting endothelial expression of adhesion_molecule for neutrophil (polymorphonuclear_leukocyte leukocyte). Preincubation of endothelial_cell with endotoxin [ lipopolysaccharide (LPS), 1 microgram/ml] led to a 4-fold increase in subsequent adherence of polymorphonuclear_leukocyte (P < 0.0001, n = 10) to endothelial_cell, an increase that was markedly attenuated when endothelial_cell were treated with dexamethasone (IC50 < 1 nM, P < 0.0001, n = 6 or 7) during preincubation with LPS. Moreover, the steroid_receptor_agonist steroid_receptor cortisol (10 microM), but not its inactive_metabolite tetrahydrocortisol (10 microM), diminished LPS-induced_endothelial_cell_adhesiveness LPS. Further evidence that the action of dexamethasone was mediated through ligation of corticosteroid_receptor [ human_glucocorticoid_receptor (hGR)] was provided by experiments utilizing the steroid_antagonist RU-486. RU-486 (10 microM), which prevents translocation of ligated hGR to the nucleus by inhibiting dissociation of hGR from heat shock protein 90, completely aborted the effect of dexamethasone on adhesiveness of endothelial_cell (P < 0.0005, n = 3). Treatment of endothelial_cell with LPS (1 microgram/ml) stimulated transcription of ELAM-1, as shown by Northern_blot_analysis, and expression of membrane-associated_ELAM-1 ELAM-1 and ICAM-1, as shown by quantitative_immunofluorescence (both P < 0.001, n = 9). Dexamethasone markedly inhibited LPS -stimulated accumulation of mRNA for ELAM-1 and expression of ELAM-1 and ICAM-1 (IC50 < 10 nM, both P < 0.001, n = 4-9); inhibition of expression by dexamethasone was reversed by RU-486 (both P < 0.005, n = 4-6). As in the adhesion studies, cortisol but not tetrahydrocortisol inhibited expression of ELAM-1 and ICAM-1 (both P < 0.005, n = 3 or 4). In contrast, sodium salicylate (1 mM) inhibited neither adhesion nor expression of these adhesion_molecule. These studies suggest that antagonism by dexamethasone of endotoxin-induced_inflammation endotoxin is a specific instance of the general biological principle that the glucocorticoid_receptor is a hormone-dependent_regulator_of_transcription.

Pax-5 encodes the transcription_factor BSAP and is expressed in B_lymphocyte, the developing CNS, and adult_testis. Later, the expression of the BSAP_gene shifts to the fetal_liver where it correlates with the onset of B_lymphopoiesis. BSAP expression persists in B_lymphocyte and is also seen in the testis of the adult_mouse. All of this evidence indicates that the transcription_factor BSAP may not only play an important role in B-cell_differentiation but also in neural_development and spermatogenesis.

calcitriol : a hematolymphopoietrope ? A nuclear_factor NF-GM2 that interacts with a regulatory_region of the GM-CSF_gene essential for its induction in responses to T-cell activation: purification from human T-cell_leukemia_line_Jurkat_cell Jurkat_cell and similarity to NF-kappa_B. Activation of T_cell by antigen, lectin, or a combination of phorbol-12-myristate_acetate (PMA) and calcium_ionophore (A23187) leads to the induction of genes for a set of lymphokine, including granulocyte-macrophage_colony-stimulating_factor (GM-CSF). Regulation of M-CSF_expression M-CSF by M-CSF : role of protein_kinase_C and transcription_factor_NF_kappa_B. macrophage-colony-stimulating_factor (M-CSF), also referred to as CSF-1, regulates the survival, growth, differentiation and functional_activity of monocyte by binding to a single class of high-affinity_cell_surface_receptor, known to be the product of the c-fms_protooncogene. The detection of both by cells of the monocyte_lineage has suggested that M-CSF may act by an autocrine_mechanism. Interestingly, it has been shown that M-CSF can induce the expression of its own gene. Although sensitivity to M-CSF can be modulated by regulation of receptor_expression and function, M-CSF_responsiveness M-CSF is largely determined at a postreceptor_level. To date, little is known about the intracellular_pathway of M-CSF_signal_transduction M-CSF. We have therefore investigated the changes in protein_kinase_C_(PKC)_activity protein_kinase_C PKC upon exposure of monocyte to M-CSF. We show that M-CSF activates and translocates PKC. Inhibition of PKC by the isoquinoline_derivative_H7 isoquinoline_derivative H7 abolishes induction of M-CSF by M-CSF. Furthermore, activation of PKC was pertussis-toxin-sensitive and was associated with the detection of an NF_kappa_B_protein in nuclear_extract of M-CSF-induced_blood_monocyte M-CSF monocyte but not in monocyte exposed to medium_treatment only. The results suggest that M-CSF induction of M-CSF involves G_protein, PKC and NF_kappa_B.

clone_pAT_133 identifies a gene that encodes another human member of a class of growth_factor-induced_gene with almost identical zinc-finger_domain zinc-finger. We report the structure and regulation of a gene represented by clone_pAT_133, which is induced upon transition from a resting_state (G0) through the early phase of the cell_cycle (G1). This difference in gene_regulation suggests distinct biological roles in the control of cell_proliferation for the respective proteins.

Our results suggest that overexpression of v-erbA v-erbA is required for its function as an oncoprotein.

anti-CD2_receptor_antibody activate the HIV_long_terminal_repeat in T_lymphocyte. reactive_oxygen_intermediate as apparently widely used messengers in the activation of the NF-kappa_B_transcription_factor NF-kappa_B transcription and HIV-1. hydrogen_peroxide and oxygen_radical are agents commonly produced during inflammatory_process. In this study, we show that micromolar_concentration of H2O2 can induce the expression and replication of HIV-1 in a human_T_cell_line. The effect is mediated by the NF-kappa_B transcription_factor transcription which is potently and rapidly activated by an H2O2_treatment H2O2 of cells from its inactive_cytoplasmic_form. N-acetyl-L-cysteine (NAC), a well characterized antioxidant which counteracts the effects of reactive_oxygen_intermediate (ROI) in living cells, prevented the activation of NF-kappa_B by H2O2. NAC and other thiol compounds also blocked the activation of NF-kappa_B by cycloheximide, double-stranded_RNA, calcium_ionophore, TNF-alpha, active_phorbol_ester, interleukin-1, lipopolysaccharide and lectin. This suggests that diverse agents thought to activate NF-kappa_B by distinct intracellular_pathway might all act through a common mechanism involving the synthesis of ROI. ROI appear to serve as messengers mediating directly or indirectly the release of the inhibitory_subunit I_kappa_B from NF-kappa_B.

Inhibition of transcription_factor transcription belonging to the rel/NF-kappa_B_family NF-kappa_B by a transdominant_negative_mutant. The KBF1_factor, which binds to the enhancer_A located in the promoter of the mouse_MHC_class_I_gene H-2Kb, is indistinguishable from the p50_DNA_binding_subunit of the transcription_factor_NF-kappa_B transcription NF-kappa_B, which regulates a series of genes involved in immune and inflammatory_response. tissue-specific_expression of the platelet_GPIIb_gene. In addition, deletion of the region containing these two domains results in a significant decrease of the promoter_activity promoter. Every enhancer works with every promoter for all the combinations tested: could new regulatory pathways evolve by enhancer_shuffling ? The promoter and enhancer of cell type-specific genes are often conserved in evolution, and hence one might expect that a given enhancer has evolved to work best with its own promoter. While this expectation may be realized in some cases, we have not found evidence for it. A total of 27 combinations of different promoter and enhancer were tested by transfection into cultured_cell. We found that the relative efficiency of the enhancer is approximately the same, irrespective of the type of promoter used, i.e., there was no strong preference for any given enhancer/promoter_combination promoter. Notably, we do not see particularly strong transcription when the immunoglobulin_kappa_enhancer (or the immunoglobulin_heavy_chain_enhancer immunoglobulin_heavy_chain) is used to activate a kappa gene promoter. We propose that a generally permissive enhancer/promoter_interaction promoter is of evolutionary benefit for higher_eukaryote : by enhancer_shuffling, genes could be easily brought under a new type of inducibility/cell_type_specificity.

Towards a molecular_understanding of T-cell_differentiation. lymphoid_differentiation is one of the best studied examples of mammalian_development. Here Hans Clevers and Michael Owen describe how the cloning of the genes that encode T-cell-specific_membrane_protein allows the identification of transcription_factor transcription that control the expression of these T-cell_gene. Such transcription_factor transcription play a key role in the development of the mature_T-cell_phenotype by functioning as 'master_regulator of T-cell_differentiation '.

A study on the circadian_rhythm of glucocorticoid_receptor. circadian_rhythm in glucocorticoid_receptor (GR) was studied in the rat_liver rat_liver_leukocyte and human_peripheral_leukocyte. For rat exposed to a natural environmental photic cycle or a 12L:12D artificial light regime, peak values of hepatic_GR were detected between 23:00 and 02:00 h. Except for a 4-hour advancement of the peak, a similar circadian_rhythm of hepatic_GR was detected in rat reared under a reversed_lighting_regimen (12D:12L; lights on between 18:30 and 06:30 h). In human_leukocyte, the peak_value of GR was found to parallel that of plasma_cortisol cortisol with high and low values detected at 04:00-08:00 h and 23:00-24:00 h, respectively. In patient suffering from Cushing's_syndrome, the circadian_rhythm of plasma cortisol either disappeared or was inverted while that of GR did not significantly deviate from the normal_subject. For apoplexic_patient patient with lesions localized to the base_of_the_brain as indicated by computerized_tomography, the diurnal_variation of GR was abolished. Conversely, diurnal rhythmicity persisted in apoplexy_patient patient whose lesions were in the cerebral_cortex. Thus, we postulated that the circadian_modification of GR was independent of the diurnal_fluctuation in plasma cortisol level or the circadian variations in environmental_lighting and that the rhythmicity might be regulated by the ' circadian_pacemaker ' located in the human_basal_brain. These diurnal variations in GR might serve to coordinate the reactivity of the target_cell to cortisol because the diurnal_rhythm of a GR-mediated_response GR, the fractional inhibition of chemotactic_migration_rate of polymorphonuclear_leukocyte by cortisol, were found to be synchronous with those of GR.

transcription_factor_requirement transcription_factor for U2_snRNA-encoding_gene_activation U2_snRNA in B_lymphoid_cell. Transcription of a human U2_small_nuclear_RNA(snRNA)-encoding_gene in HeLa_cell requires a distal_enhancer_element, which is composed of one octamer_motif (Oct) and three Sp_1-binding_site. To study the transcription_factor_requirement transcription_factor in B-cell, different U2_enhancer_construction were transfected into the lymphoid_cell_line, BJA-B. The results showed that the activation of U2 snRNA transcription in B-cell also requires an enhancer comprising both the Oct and at least one Sp_1-binding_site. Deletion of all the Sp_1-binding_site from the enhancer reduces transcription by 80-90% in HeLa, as well as in BJA-B_cell, whereas the removal of the octamer-binding_site reduces transcription to levels below detection in both cell types. Enhancers containing a single Oct have, nevertheless, the capacity to partially activate U2_snRNA_transcription U2_snRNA in both HeLa_cell, in which only OTF-1 is expressed, and in BJA-B_cell in which OTF-2 is the predominantly expressed octamer-binding_factor. The most likely interpretation of our results is that both the ubiquitous transcription_factor, OTF-1, and the B-cell-specific_transcription_factor transcription_factor, OTF-2, can activate U2_snRNA_transcription U2_snRNA. The results also revealed a similar functional cooperation between the transcription factors which bind to the Oct and the adjacent Sp_1-binding_site in BJA-B_cell, as has been observed in HeLa_cell, since a template which contains a weak binding site for OTF expresses wild-type_level of U2_snRNA in both cell types when the weak octamer-binding_site is combined with a Sp_1-binding_site.

One base pair change abolishes the T_cell-restricted_activity of a kB-like_proto-enhancer_element from the interleukin_2_promoter. The inducible, T_cell-specific_enhancer of murine_and_human_Interleukin_2_(Il-2)_gene Il-2 contain the kB-like_sequence GGGATTTCACC as an essential_cis-acting_enhancer_motif. When cloned in multiple copies this so-called TCEd (distal_T_cell_element) acts as an inducible proto-enhancer_element in E14_T_lymphoma_cel, but not in HeLa_cell. In extracts of induced, Il-2_secreting_El4_cell Il-2 three individual protein_factor bind to TCEd_DNA. The binding of the most prominent factor, named TCF-1 (T_cell_factor_1), is correlated with the proto-enhancer_activity of TCEd. TCF-1 consists of two polypeptide of about 50_kD and 105_kD ; the former seems to be related to the 50_kD_polypeptide of NF-kB. purified_NF-kB is also able to bind to the TCEd, but TCF-1 binds stronger than NF-kB to TCEd DNA. The conversion of the TCEd to a 'perfect'_NF-kB_binding_site NF-kB leads to a tighter binding of NF-kB to TCEd_DNA TCEd and, as a functional consequence, to the activity of the 'converted'_TCEd_motif TCEd in HeLa_cell. Thus, the substitution of the underlined A residue to a C within the GGGATTTCACC_motif abolishes its T_cell-restricted_activity and leads to its functioning in both El4_cell and HeLa_cell. These results indicate that lymphocyte-specific factors binding to the TCEd are involved in the control of T_cell_specific-transcription of the Il-2_gene Il-2.

An erythroid_specific_enhancer upstream to the gene encoding the cell-type_specific_transcription_factor transcription_factor GATA-1. The transcription_factor GATA-1 is expressed in a subset of hemopoietic_cell, where it mediates the cell-type_specific_expression of several genes. We have cloned the mouse and human GATA-1_gene. A region upstream to the first exon, and highly conserved between mouse and man, acts as an erythroid_specific_enhancer in transient_assay, if linked to the GATA-1 or to the SV40_promoter. The activity of the enhancer is almost completely dependent on the integrity of a dimeric_GATA-1_binding_site.

Demonstration of a 1,25-dihydroxyvitamin_D3-responsive_protein 1,25-dihydroxyvitamin_D3 in human_lymphocyte : immunologic_crossreactivity and inverse regulation with the vitamin_D_receptor. Using Western blot analysis with a monoclonal_antibody recognizing a 17-amino_acid_epitope of the 1,25-dihydroxyvitamin_D3_[1,25(OH)2D3]receptor 1,25-dihydroxyvitamin_D3 1,25(OH)2D3, we have detected two crossreacting_protein in activated_normal_human_lymphocyte human_lymphocyte. The smaller of the two proteins(50_kDa) was indistinguishable from the classical 1,25(OH)2D3_receptor 1,25(OH)2D3 and, similar to the classical 1,25(OH)2D3_receptor 1,25(OH)2D3, was upregulated in a dose-dependent fashion by 1,25(OH)2D3. The larger crossreacting protein exhibited an electrophoretic_mobility of 80_kDa, was localized in the cell_cytosol, and appeared to be specific for activated_lymphocyte since it was not detected in several other human_cell including monocyte. Recently, the development of monoclonal antibodies directed against ER has been applied to the study of breast_carcinoma and results obtained show good correlation with the quantitative_SBA SBA. We studied 49 cases of B-cell_chronic_lymphocytic_leukemia (CLL) using immunostaining of cytospin_preparation. In 30 of these cases ER_enzyme_immunoassay ER (ER-EIA ER) was also performed. cultured_MCF-7_cell, derived from a pleural_effusion of a breast_cancer_patient, known to contain high levels of ER were used as a positive control (40-48% ER_positive_cell ER by immunocytochemistry; 200 fmol/mg protein by EIA). All of the CLL_case CLL except two (96%) were negative for ER (less than 1% staining; less than 4 fmol/mg protein). The two positive cases expressed granular_ER_staining ER over the nucleus (9.2 and 12.1% positive cells) and were positive by EIA and SBA. It is concluded that (i) patient with CLL rarely express ER and (ii) immunocytochemical_staining of cytospin_preparation is a valid technique for the measurement of ER. It is of interest that one of the positive cases was diagnosed as CLL with Richter's_transformation confirming earlier findings.

Two glucocorticoid_binding_site on the human_glucocorticoid_receptor. glucocorticoid are known to have a lytic effect in leukemic_cell via interactions with the glucocorticoid_receptor (GR). cortisol and various synthetic_glucocorticoid bind to the GR with one-site_kinetics. cortivazol (CVZ) is a unique, high potency synthetic_glucocorticoid, which has a phenylpyrazol fused to the A-ring of the steroid_nucleus and displays binding consistent with two or more sites in the cytosol from CEM_C7_cell (a human_acute_lymphoblastic_T-cell_line). It has previously been shown that the lower affinity class of sites are similar in affinity and site_molarity to those recognized by dexamethasone. The higher_affinity_site affinity bind CVZ with 20- to 50-fold greater affinity, consistent with CVZ 's enhanced biological_effect. In mutant leukemic_cell resistant to the lytic effects of dexamethasone, CVZ both lyses the cells and recognizes a single class of sites similar to the high affinity site in CEM_C7_cell. We have carried out experiments to define the nature of the higher_affinity_CVZ_binding_site affinity CVZ. We now show that: 1) CVZ has more than one binding site in a second, independent, B-cell_line, IM-9 ; 2) the antiglucocorticoid RU_38486 is able to block both CVZ 's higher and lower affinity sites; 3) all of CVZ's_binding_site CVZ are on a protein immunologically indistinguishable from the human GR ; and 4) freshly isolated clones of CVZ -resistant cells have lost all binding sites for CVZ. These data indicate that CVZ is recognizing two glucocorticoid_binding_site on the human GR or a protein very similar to it.

pseudohypoaldosteronism in eight families: different forms of inheritance are evidence for various genetic_defect. pseudohypoaldosteronism is a rare hereditary_disorder presenting in early infancy with renal_salt_loss leading to hyponatremia and hyperkalemia despite high levels of plasma_aldosterone. The patient are insensitive to mineralocorticoid ; however, sodium_supplementation sodium is able to correct electrolyte_abnormality. Absent or greatly diminished type I_aldosterone_receptor in peripheral_mononuclear_leucocyte have been recently demonstrated and explain the lack of response to mineralocorticoid. We have studied the mode of inheritance in eight families with a total of nine patient. There was evidence for an autosomal_recessive_form of inheritance in four families, while the other four families appeared to have an autosomal_dominant_mode of transmission. In three families the autosomal_recessive_form was characterized by normal_receptor as well as hormone data in both parents, while in one family receptor_level in both parents were greatly reduced, but hormone_level were normal. In the four families with an autosomal_dominant_mode of transmission there was always one parent with reduced_receptor_binding in peripheral_mononuclear_leucocyte and elevated serum_hormone_level hormone_level. These parent were entirely asymptomatic. In an extended family we were able to study an aunt and her newborn daughter, who were both also biochemically affected but clinically_asymptomatic. It, therefore, appears that this dual pattern of genetic_transmission may indicate differing genetic_defect which cause the same clinical picture of pseudohypoaldosteronism.

Higher NK_activity could be predicted by the perception of high quality emotional_support from a spouse or intimate_other, perceived social support from the patient's_physician, estrogen_receptor-negative_tumor_status estrogen_receptor estrogen, having an excisional_biopsy as surgical_treatment, and actively seeking social_support as a major coping strategy (R2 = 0.33, F(5,55) = 5.5, p less than 0.0004). Moreover, there is no cooperation or synergy between R and EB1 when activating the B_domain (ZRE-B plus the R-responsive_element) positioned as an enhancer. We have tested several subregions of the DR_enhancer B_domain, either alone or in combination, for their capacity to transmit the R-activating_signal to the rabbit_beta-globin_promoter. One of the protoenhancer contains the overlapping_palindrome 5'-TTGTCCcgtGGACAAaTGTCC-3'. However, one palindrome, either alone or duplicated, or the overlapping_palindrome did not respond to R.

circadian_rhythm of glucocorticoid_receptor in human_peripheral_leukocyte and their reactivity to glucocorticoid. 1) There exists a CR of GR in human_leukocyte, PMN, and monocyte with the peak values from 0400 to 0800 hr and the trough values between 2300 and 0000 hr. In this study, we demonstrate reconstitution of a cell-free_processing_system and demonstrate directly that: (a) the ubiquitin-_proteasome_system ubiquitin proteasome is involved in processing of the intact p105 precursor, (b) conjugation of ubiquitin to the precursor is an essential intermediate step in the processing, (c) the recently discovered novel species of the ubiquitin-carrier_protein ubiquitin, E2-F1, that is involved in the conjugation and degradation of p53, is also required for the limited processing of the p105_precursor, and (d) a novel, approximately 320-kDa_specie of ubiquitin-protein_ligase ubiquitin-protein_ligase ubiquitin, is involved in the process. OBJECTIVE: To investigate the long-term effects of treatment with low doses of flutamide on clinical and hormonal_parameter, as well as on the androgen_receptor status, in hirsute_women.
